issues.detail: The Hebrew 'כִּי יָבוֹא כַנָּהָר צָר רוּחַ יְהוָה נֹסְסָה בוֹ' means 'for the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him' (or similar: 'the adversary comes like a river, the Spirit of the LORD raises a banner against him'). The Chinese omits the word 'צָר' (adversary/enemy) and the phrase 'נֹסְסָה בוֹ' (raises a standard against him), instead rendering only 'the Spirit of the LORD will come swiftly like a great river,' which changes the meaning: the Hebrew has the enemy coming like a flood and the Spirit opposing him, not the Spirit itself coming like a flood.
